questions.question: In a patient who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, on which postoperative day would you first consider the diagnosis of heparin‑induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) if the platelet count begins to fall before POD 5, and what prior exposure explains this early onset?

Describe the pathogenic mechanism by which autoimmune heparin‑induced thrombocytopenia (aHIT) antibodies activate platelets in the absence of heparin, highlighting the role of PF4‑antibody complexes and FcγRIIA receptors.

A postoperative cardiac surgery patient presents with severe thrombocytopenia (nadir 13 ×10⁹/L), normal hemoglobin trend, normal haptoglobin, and no schistocytes on blood film. Which of the following conditions is LEAST likely to account for these findings?
A) Post‑transfusion purpura
B) Sepsis‑associated consumptive coagulopathy
C) Heparin‑induced thrombocytopenia
D) Drug‑induced immune thrombocytopenia from vancomycin
E) Disseminated intravascular coagulation secondary to massive bleeding

In a patient with suspected aHIT who has just suffered an acute ischemic stroke and has a platelet count <30 ×10⁹/L, which non‑heparin anticoagulant is most appropriate for immediate initiation and why?

The serotonin‑release assay (SRA) performed on this patient’s serum shows >95% serotonin release at 0 U/mL heparin, >95% release at therapeutic heparin concentrations (0.1–0.3 U/mL), complete inhibition at supratherapeutic heparin (100 U/mL), and only 76% inhibition when the FcγRIIA‑blocking monoclonal antibody IV.3 is added at 0.1 U/mL heparin. What do these findings indicate about the nature of the patient’s anti‑PF4 antibodies?

During treatment for aHIT this patient’s fibrinogen fell from >6 g/L to ~2.5 g/L while d‑dimer levels rose dramatically and schistocytes appeared on peripheral smear after day 9. How do these laboratory trends reflect the underlying pathophysiology of HIT‑associated consumptive coagulopathy?
Why was antithrombin concentrate administered before initiating therapeutic‑dose fondaparinux in this case, and how does antithrombin status affect fondaparinux efficacy?

High‑dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) is often used in refractory aHIT. Explain its proposed mechanism of action in this setting and discuss why the patient’s platelet count rose only modestly despite three consecutive 100‑g doses.
